title: Tamsin and the Choir
premise: Lior Thackeray, a bone-carver who hears the dead, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things — until the old gods begin answering prayers again and the ledger entries start writing themselves. With Tamsin, a choirgirl whose voice can bind or unbind divine covenants, Lior discovers the gods were never silent by choice: a guild faction has been harvesting their voices for profit. To reforge the broken covenant between realms, Lior must choose between exposing the Guild's crimes and protecting the only family he has left; in the end he burns the ledgers, frees the Choir of the old gods with Tamsin's final song, and accepts exile as the price of a truth no law will honor.
about_author: Sebastian Crane is the pen name of a former cathedral archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval choir manuscripts before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about institutions, memory, and the people who keep the books nobody is supposed to read.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Wrote Back
chapters.summary: POV Lior. In the Vellum Guild's counting house, Lior carves bones for clients and records trades in impossible things. One night an entry appears in his own handwriting that he never wrote: 'The gods are awake. Payment due.' He hears a dead choirboy humming beneath the floorboards. Emotional beat: unease — the meticulous keeper of records realizes the record is keeping him.

chapters.title: A Girl Who Sings to Locked Doors
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Tamsin, a choirgirl at the Cathedral of the Quiet Bell, notices her hymns open doors that should stay shut — and that the senior clergy flinch when she sings certain verses. She follows a thread of song into the Guild quarter and collides with Lior fleeing his haunted ledger. Emotional beat: wary recognition — two outsiders hearing the same forbidden music.

chapters.title: What the Dead Charge for Answers
chapters.summary: POV Lior. Lior bargains with the dead choirboy, who reveals the gods' voices were sold off in installments decades ago — the Guild's founding fortune. The price of the truth is a memory Lior treasures: his mother's face. He pays it and immediately doubts what he's lost. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Provost's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Guild Provost Aldous Vane takes Tamsin under his wing, offering protection, patronage, and a warm lie: that the gods abandoned the world willingly and the Guild merely kept their leavings. Tamsin, orphaned and hungry for belonging, almost believes him. Emotional beat: seduction of comfort — loyalty offered by the man who must be exposed.

chapters.title: Nine Names in the Bone
chapters.summary: POV Lior. Decoding the ledger, Lior finds nine god-names carved into a single femur — the covenant's original terms, including a clause: the covenant renews only if spoken by a living voice that both realms trust. Every clue points to a singer. He realizes Tamsin is the key, and that telling her makes her a target. Emotional beat: dread of responsibility.

chapters.title: The Harvest at Vespers
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. During vespers, Guild harvesters move on the cathedral to take Tamsin's voice before she can be sworn to anything. The dead choirboy warns her mid-hymn; she escapes through a door her own song unlocks, but her mentor is taken in her place. Emotional beat: guilt and fury — comfort was always a trap.

chapters.title: Exiles' Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Lior. Hiding in the bone-carver's slum, Lior and Tamsin weigh their options: flee, bargain with Vane, or break into the Vault of Voices where the stolen god-songs are stored. Lior calculates every path ends in betrayal of someone; Tamsin refuses to do arithmetic with lives. Their alliance cracks and reforges into real trust. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: The Vault of Voices
chapters.summary: POV alternating. They breach the Vault and find the gods' voices bottled in wax cylinders of carved bone — and find Vane waiting, who offers Lior restoration of his mother's memory in exchange for walking away. Lior refuses, choosing truth over the last warmth of his past. Tamsin begins the unbinding song as alarms rise. Emotional beat: sacrifice made irrevocable.

chapters.title: Covenant
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin, climax. As Guild enforcers close in, Tamsin sings the nine names while the freed voices of the old gods pour through the cathedral like weather. The covenant reforges itself around her voice; Vane, caught between realms mid-lie, is unmade by the truths he sold. Lior holds the door against the harvesters, bleeding, keeping time with his carving knife on stone. Emotional beat: terrible, triumphant renewal.

chapters.title: The Empty Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Lior, resolution. The Guild falls outside any court — its charter voided by the renewed covenant, its members scattered by justice no magistrate delivered. Lior burns the ledgers rather than let them become weapons again, keeps one blank book, and leaves the city with Tamsin, who now hums with nine voices. He still cannot recall his mother's face, but the dead sing to him kindly now. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — truth kept at a cost worth paying.
